claims.statement: EHDS phases patient summaries and prescriptions into exchange by 2029 and lab results, imaging and discharge reports by 2031, creating future interoperability work for health-data holders and EHR vendors.
EHDS establishes common EHR rules and mandatory harmonized interoperability and logging components, but implementing specifications and Polish procurement routes remain material unknowns.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Private laboratory CIO, EHR product head or clinic network operations director
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Lab-specific terminology mapping, data-quality monitoring and migration tooling; EHR vendors can internalize
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future ownership by the prospective business under direct laboratory or EHR-vendor contracts
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: EHR vendors, laboratory-information-system integrators and health IT consultants

fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Milestone implementation billing plus annual support prepaid
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 50-70% after clinical informatics and security costs
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Integration engineering, clinical terminology review and on-call support
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: GDPR counsel, security certification, insurance and medical-software classification review
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Integration license, implementation and annual monitoring
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Secure cloud, terminology licenses, integration and clinical specialist time

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: EHR/LIS incumbents add native EHDS export and logging modules
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Paid interoperability implementation or avoided failed exchange/rework when lab data must enter EHDS-compatible records
commercial_mechanics.payer: Private laboratory network, clinic group or EHR/LIS vendor
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: 2029-2031 roadmap, EHR replacement or failed interoperability test
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual monitoring, specification changes and new interfaces

contrary_evidence: National infrastructure may absorb much of the normalization layer.
Clinical integrations have long sales and certification cycles.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: No present health-data rights; proposed data-processing and workflow-integration agreements
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Use synthetic data for conformance tools or sell to an EHR vendor instead of providers
critical_control_point.current_owner: Patients and health providers hold data rights; EHR/LIS vendors control source systems
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future ownership by the prospective business under direct laboratory or EHR-vendor contracts
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Medical-student relationship provides no patient, clinic or university data rights
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business only after data-processing agreements and security validation
critical_control_point.subject: Laboratory-result normalization and conformance layer

economics.acquisition_route: Build synthetic-data conformance tests, win one paid readiness assessment, then integrate through an established LIS partner
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 60 institutions at 180,000 PLN ARR-equivalent and 22% EBITDA yields about 2.4m PLN EBITDA; 4-6x supports 5m+ founder value in years 8-12. Procurement and certification may extend timing.
economics.founder_time: 20-25 hours weekly for prototypes; full clinical deployment likely requires leaving employment after traction
economics.gross_margin_basis: License and support less secure hosting, integration and clinical review
economics.payback: Assumption: 3-5 institutional implementations repay initial build in 24-36 months
economics.pricing: Assumption: 80,000-250,000 PLN implementation plus 40,000-180,000 PLN annual monitoring
economics.retention_or_repeat: Sticky interfaces, continuing quality monitoring and evolving specifications

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: De-identified mapping rules and conformance-test corpus
fingerprint.customer: Polish private labs, clinics and EHR/LIS vendors
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Health-data system owner pays at readiness and interface go-live
fingerprint.problem_trigger: EHDS exchange deadlines expose inconsistent laboratory semantics

founder_fit: Biosignal, health and data backgrounds align.
Synthetic-data validation can start without sensitive access.
High compliance load is a meaningful drawback.

structure.control_point: Validated lab-normalization mappings inside exchange workflow
structure.critical_dependency: EHR/LIS integration and lawful health-data processing

thesis: Future state: Polish laboratory results move across EHDS-compatible systems in standardized form. The missing technical mechanism is a validated normalization, logging and conformance node between heterogeneous LIS/EHR systems.
title: EHDS Laboratory-Normalization Node
